title: Thread a hotel ball-top hanger into a free-swinging captive closet ring and drop its stem into the seat
instruction: Hang the wooden ball-top hanger in the chrome closet ring on the rail, then let go.
context: Most hotel travelers know anti-theft ball-top hangers: they have no hook and hang only in a loose captive ring on the closet rod. One arm must catch and steady the free-sliding, free-swinging ring while the other threads the ball through its keyhole and drops the stem into the seat, unlike open-hook hanger or fixed-peg hanging tasks.
setup: cm from arm-base midpoint, x forward, y left, z above the oak table. Closet bay, fixed dark walnut plywood: two side walls 11.3 x 1.8 x 30 cm tall (x 35.4 to 46.7, inner faces y +-35.0), back panel 1.2 x 73.6 x 30 cm (front face x 45.5), and fixed 3.2 cm OD chrome steel rod (70 cm long) along y at x 37.0, z 25.0. Captive ball-top security ring (National Hospitality Supply CPJRNG chrome steel J-ring, rods to 1.5 in; 40 g) on the rod at y +4.5, free to slide y -31.2 to +31.2 and swing +-54 deg: 7.35 cm overall: 3.8 cm ID chrome upper loop (4.3 cm OD, 1.0 cm wide) above a centered 3.2 x 4.5 x 3.05 cm steel keyhole housing with a 1.9 cm wide x 1.8 cm tall upper front window above a 0.9 cm lower stem slot and inner cradle ledges. Valet tray, fixed charcoal wood: 5.65 x 44.0 x 0.8 cm base centered at x 22.6, y -4.0, front lip 1.6 cm tall at x 21.0, two rear pillars (1.8 x 2.4 x 5.4 cm) at y -18.5 and +10.5 leaving an open center bay. Wooden ball-top suit hanger (National Hospitality Supply CPP88, 140 g design mass, natural solid hardwood, 43.1 cm span, 1.59 cm (5/8 in) thick, 20 deg shoulders, 1.0 cm pant bar, 1.6 cm chrome ball on a 0.6 cm stem, no hook) leans 12 deg back in the tray with its ball at x 24.5, y -4.0, z 14.2.
scoring: After release (pads >= 3 cm away) and parts still (<1.5 cm/s, <0.15 rad/s) 2.0 s. D: hanger low point >2 cm below table 0.5 s = 0.0. E: ball centre in keyhole pocket 0.3 s. Seated: ball within 8 mm front-back, 6 mm along rod of slot centre, on ledges, hanger >= 3.5 cm above table. Ledges read as drop H within -3.4/+3.6 mm of H0 (hand-seated; sim 100.9 mm; perched reads 9.4 mm short); real trials log perched H_p, band valid if H0-H_p >= 7 mm, else pull test: lift 4 mm (or half H0-H_p if <8 mm), draw 10 mm forward <2 N (scale), ball stays. Sim/real H0 set separately (README). 1.0: Seated, tilt <=18 deg, ring swing <=15 deg, walls >=0.5 cm, released, still, no D. 0.5: as 1.0 but tilt 18-35, swing 15-30, or wall <0.5 cm. 0.25: E, released, still, no D, not Seated within 0.5 limits. 0.0: D, held, moving, draped on rod, no E, idle. Real: caliper H, ruler, photos, video.
reset_notes: Lift the hanger 1 cm to align the ball with the upper keyhole window, draw it forward out of the ring, set it leaning 12 deg back in the valet tray against the rear pillars, and slide the ring back to the y +4.5 cm tape mark on the rod.
fidelity: Rigid wood and metal. Ring on chained slide/hinge joints on the rod axis (3 mm radial clearance), not loose contact. Commercial: ring ID 38 mm, hanger 17 in x 5/8 in, flat fixed bar. Design values: ring 73.5 mm, 40 g, keyhole 19 x 18 mm, slot 9 mm, depth 7 mm, ledges 49.5 mm below rod; hanger 140 g, ball 16 mm, stem 6 mm; 1-1.5 mm/side clearance. Bench-measure real ring; re-derive keyhole if off >1 mm; calibrate H0, H_p (README).
scores: Dream-1 run: 0 (reached the rod with the right hand, held the hanger tilted near the ring, did not hang it); demo: 1 (lifted hanger from tray, passed it to the rod with both arms, hung it, released, backed away)
